questions.question: Which generation strategy lets Hibernate reserve a block of ids in advance, so inserts can be batched?
options: SEQUENCE
IDENTITY
Assigned ids
No strategy at all
questions.explanation: A sequence can hand out ids before the insert, while IDENTITY only learns the id after the insert runs.

questions.question: Why might a team choose UUID primary keys?
options: UUIDs are smaller than Long values
UUIDs are always sorted in creation order
Ids can be created outside the database, will not clash across servers and are hard to guess
UUIDs need no primary key column
questions.explanation: A UUID is random and created in Java, which suits many systems, at the cost of bigger indexes.

questions.question: A Ward entity has an assigned String id and no @GeneratedValue. The code saves Ward("ICU", 12) and then Ward("ICU", 20). How many rows are in the table?
options: Two rows with the same code
One row, because the second save updates the existing ICU row
Zero rows
The second save throws a duplicate key error
questions.explanation: With an assigned id, Spring Data checks the database and updates the row if the id already exists.

questions.question: A developer wants ids that start at 1000 and grow by one, but uses a plain @GeneratedValue with no generator. What is the problem?
options: IDENTITY columns cannot be used with Long
The id field must be a String
UUID is required for numbering
The default sequence starts at 1, so a @SequenceGenerator with initialValue is needed
questions.explanation: Start values are set on a @SequenceGenerator with initialValue, and allocationSize = 1 keeps the ids in order.

questions.question: An app shows order pages at /orders/41 for every user and checks nothing else. Why is a sequential id a problem here?
options: Users can guess other ids, so the server must also check ownership
Sequential ids are not unique
Sequential ids make the entity final
Hibernate refuses to load ids below 100
questions.explanation: Ids are not secrets. Always check on the server that the user may see the row, and use UUIDs when guessing must be hard.
